title: Integrated Plant Health, Scouting and Diagnostic Reasoning
summary: Integrated plant health combines prevention, repeatable scouting, evidence-based diagnosis and compatible controls; symptoms are observations that must be separated from the causal diagnosis before intervention.

sections.title: Scouting is a measurement system
sections.body: Repeatable routes, sampling effort, location records and severity categories allow plant-health observations to be compared through time. Recording negative as well as positive findings helps distinguish true change from a change in how intensely the crop was inspected.

sections.title: Symptoms can have biological and abiotic look-alikes
sections.body: Wilting, chlorosis, lesions or stunting can arise from pests, pathogens, nutrients, roots, irrigation or environment. Strong diagnosis begins with distribution and progression and adds microscopy, laboratory testing or controlled observations when the consequence of being wrong is high.

sections.title: Integrated control includes outcome review
sections.body: Sanitation, clean stock, environmental management, cultural controls and legally permitted biological or other interventions can work together. Follow-up scouting should use the same baseline method so efficacy is measured rather than assumed from product claims.
